violation: magelib has zero test files. `find . -name '*_test.go'` returns 0 across the repo, so `mage test` reports `[no test files]` and exits 0: a green gate that tests nothing, the same shape as GAPI-DIV-042's empty fuzz corpus. This is the library implementing Lint, Doctor, CheckHermetic, BufGenerate and Release for the entire ecosystem, so every gate in gapi and goblin is enforced by untested code, and MAGELIB-DIV-002 is a direct consequence: a defect in the schema treaty's baseline selection survived because nothing exercised it. Separately, none of magelib's own targets call CheckHermetic - Build, Test and Lint go straight to `go build`, `go test` and magelib.Lint - while both consumer repos gate their equivalents on it (goblin Magefile.go TestCluster does `mg.Deps(checkHermetic)`). The hermeticity rule the library exists to enforce is the one rule it does not apply to itself. Ledger note: this repo's divergence.jsonl and deprecation.jsonl were both 0 bytes, which read as a clean repo and meant an unkept one.
rule: go-project-manifesto (behavior is tested at public interfaces; a target asserting nothing must not report success); build-environment.md (targets run through the pinned shell)

violation: The schema treaty could not fail in CI. BufGenerate ran `buf breaking` against whatever baseline its callers hardcoded, and both callers pass `.git#ref=HEAD` (gapi/Magefile.go:203, goblin/Magefile.go:189). That baseline is correct for a developer comparing an edited working tree against the last commit and inert anywhere the working tree IS the commit: on a fresh CI checkout buf compares the schema against itself. Demonstrated in goblin with `string method = 2` retyped to `int64` in proto/goblin/v1/rpc.proto: `buf breaking --against .git#ref=HEAD` on the dirty tree exits 100 with the field-level message, while `buf breaking --against .` on the identical tree exits 0. Any CI job wrapped around `mage proto` before this was fixed would have been green by construction, installing review-v2 finding 1's exact pathology into the mechanism the ecosystem manifesto names as the treaty between repos. GOBLIN-DIV-036 compounds it: the payloads buf would police are JSON, so even a correct baseline sees only the envelope.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (buf breaking is the schema treaty between repos); go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate)

violation: The hermeticity guarantee stops exactly where the gate's real work begins. CheckHermetic verifies that `go`, `gcc` and `protoc` - plus `pandoc` when it is present on PATH - resolve under /nix/store, then checks the toolchain pin. It does not check `buf`, `golangci-lint` or `gosec`. Since 1430285 wired `mg.Deps(checkHermetic)` to Build, Test and Lint, Lint now guarantees a hermetic Go toolchain and then shells out to three tools none of which were checked: golangci-lint and gosec directly (lint.go), buf via BufGenerate (proto.go). Each of the three could come from anywhere on PATH, including a host install. A host golangci-lint of a different version silently changes what the lint gate enforces; a host buf silently changes the schema treaty MAGELIB-DIV-002 exists to keep honest. What makes this an entry rather than a footnote is the asymmetry: `DoctorConfig.SharedTools` exists precisely so a repo can extend the hermetic tool list, and this repo's own Magefile.go passes buf, golangci-lint, gosec, govulncheck, mage and goimports to Doctor, which feeds them to checkHermeticResolution. So the doctor checks these tools and the gate that depends on them does not - and the doctor is advisory, run when an operator asks, while Lint runs in CI on every push. CheckHermetic takes no parameter through which a caller could close the gap.
rule: build-environment.md (targets run through the pinned shell; hermetic resolution comes from the pinned store); go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate - one whose enforcing tools are unpinned reports a result it did not control)
exit: RESOLVED 2026-07-31. Closes on the GATE, demonstrated failing in all three repos. THE GATE: CheckHermetic is now variadic and each repo calls it as `magelib.CheckHermetic(toolchain.SharedTools...)`, where `toolchain` is a single package-level DoctorConfig var that `Doctor` also reads. One value, two readers, so the advisory diagnostic and the enforcing check cannot report different tool sets - which is the drift this entry named. The gate runs from every target carrying mg.Deps(checkHermetic) and reaches CI through required contexts in all three repos. THE PROOF, run per repo and identical in shape: a real executable wrapper for golangci-lint placed ahead of the store copy on PATH. Gated, the target stops at checkHermetic with "golangci-lint resolves outside the Nix store" and the lint gate's own output never appears. With checkHermetic reverted to CheckHermetic() and nothing else changed, the identical command PASSES and the shadowed binary runs the lint - instrumented in goblin so that "it passed" could not be mistaken for "the shadow ran". Restored byte-identical each time and the failure returned. The failure alone would only show a gate exists; the pair shows this change is what made it catch anything. A wrapper and not a symlink, because checkStorePath calls EvalSymlinks and a symlink into /nix/store resolves back and passes. CI: magelib run 30662416726 (60 tests, 3 checkHermetic dependency lines), gapi pull request 32 (5 of 5 required checks), goblin pull request 15 (5 of 5, including Cluster E2E with criu in the gated set). The consumers were bumped to magelib v0.3.0 and re-vendored, proven by grepping the variadic signature INSIDE vendor/ rather than by a green build - go.work satisfies the new symbol from ../magelib even when vendoring did nothing - and confirmed under the mode that ships with `GOWORK=off go vet -mod=vendor -tags mage .`, which plain `go build ./...` cannot do because the Magefile sits behind the mage build tag. Widening the set was safe by construction rather than by luck: Doctor's hermetic-resolution check already ran checkHermeticResolution over the same SharedTools list, so the gate cannot fail where doctor succeeds, and doctor was run first in each repo to confirm it. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN, recorded rather than solved: nothing asserts `toolchain` stays wired to checkHermetic. Changing that call back to CheckHermetic() leaves every target green and every Magefile compiling, and Magefile.go is //go:build mage and outside the package graph, so no test in pkg/magelib can reach it - the same residual MAGELIB-DIV-001, GAPI-DIV-044 and GOBLIN-DIV-045 all record for their own wiring. The checked set is still a LIST: a target that starts shelling out to some new tool does not fail for having skipped it, it just leaves the list quietly incomplete, which is this entry's own finding recurring one tool later. checkStorePath falls back to the unresolved PATH entry when filepath.EvalSymlinks returns an error, so a tool whose symlink cannot be read is judged on where it was found rather than where it points, and a /nix/store-prefixed link to somewhere else passes. And doctor.go's checkHermeticResolution still spells out the same base-plus-extras concatenation that hermeticTools now expresses, minus the pandoc probe - two spellings of one decision, which is how a divergence of this shape starts.

surface: pkg/magelib/terminology.go (CheckTerminology skip parsing), pkg/magelib/filelength.go (CheckFileLength skip parsing)
violation: Both shared gates can be silently disabled by a plausible configuration value, and the two defects are one defect at two sites: the skip-parsing logic is duplicated between CheckTerminology and CheckFileLength, and it has already drifted. (1) CheckTerminology's bare-name skip branch is unvalidated. Its PATH branch validates properly and carries the correct reasoning verbatim - 'A skip that silently matches nothing, or silently matches everything, is worse than no skip at all: the gate goes quiet and quiet is indistinguishable from clean' - and rejects '.', '..' and absolute paths. One else-branch away, a bare name is taken as `skipNames[n] = true` with no checks. WalkDir's root entry is named '.', so `CheckTerminology(rules, ".")` prunes the entire tree and returns nil. Measured 2026-08-01 against a tree containing the forbidden phrase: with no skip the gate catches it; with a bare '.' skip it reports clean. CheckFileLength guards exactly this case, because the agent building it noticed the hole while copying the pattern - so the ecosystem's newest gate is safe and its oldest is not. (2) CheckFileLength accepts any path as a skip without justification. It rejects a path claimed as BOTH waiver and skip, but a path claimed only as a skip passes unquestioned, and nothing in the mechanism distinguishes generated code the rule exempts from hand-written code someone wanted to stop hearing about. Demonstrated 2026-08-01: moving goblin's 1200-line supervisor.go from its waiver list to its skip list leaves the gate green and silent about the file. A waiver is debt that must shrink; a skip is permanent. Reclassifying the first as the second is undetectable, and a reviewer sees only a line moved between two string slices. gapi's skip has an external alibi in gopy's non-standard header; the next skip added anywhere may not.
rule: go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate; fail loudly at boundaries); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (shared mechanisms are the contract - a gate the ecosystem depends on must not be disableable by its own configuration)
exit: Close on a GATE, and on ONE parser rather than two agreeing parsers. The root cause is duplication: each gate re-implements skip parsing, they have already drifted, and a third gate would repeat the choice. Extract a single validated skip primitive that every gate consumes, so a skip that cannot mean what the caller intended is rejected once, for all of them, and correctness is not a property each new gate has to rediscover. Two things must then hold and both must be mechanically checked. (1) Every gate rejects a bare skip of '', '.' and '..'. The test is table-driven ACROSS the gates rather than written per gate - a per-gate test is the same duplication one level up and would have let this drift happen again. Demonstrated by removing the guard and showing the test fail, not by the guard existing. (2) A skip carries a required reason, so adding one means stating why the rule does not reach that path. That does not make a wrong reason impossible, but it makes the claim reviewable: 'gopy output, non-standard generated header' is checkable, while a bare path in a slice is not. The waiver/skip distinction only works if the classification is auditable at the point it is made. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN: a fourth gate added to magelib with its own skip handling, which is exactly how these two diverged - the newest gate is safe only because one agent happened to notice while copying. Nothing structurally prevents the next one from starting fresh, and a shared primitive is only shared while everyone uses it. Note also that requiring a reason string is a breaking API change for both consumers, so it needs a tag and a re-vendor in gapi and goblin, and their existing skip entries need reasons written for them rather than backfilled with 'legacy'.
